chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kumaydani and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The honor of the believer is his night prayer, and his glory is refraining from bothering the people.
ai.seo_question: What are the two main sources of a believer's honor and glory according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a concise definition of the believer's dual nobility, linking vertical devotion (Qiyam al-Layl) with horizontal social ethics (Kaf al-Adha). In Shia tradition, night prayer is not merely ritual but the source of spiritual strength that enables one to restrain oneself from harming others, thus fulfilling the rights of creation through the power of worship.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-18 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Abi Ja’far al-Kumaydany and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
A believer’s honor is in night prayers, and his glory is in not bothering the people.”
